title: BA2/286/2022 of JAVED ALI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Second Bail Application No. 286 of 2022
Javed Ali ........Applicant

Present:-
Mr. Rajendra Singh Azad, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. with Ms. Sonika Khulbe, Brief
Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Applicant Javed Ali is in judicial custody in
FIR/Case Crime No.81 of 2021, under Sections 332, 353
IPC and Sections 8/22 of the Narcotic Drugs and
Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, Police Station Piran
Kaliyar, District Haridwar. He has sought his release on
bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. This is the second bail application. The first
bail application of the applicant has been rejected on
18.11.2021.
4. According to the FIR, on 15.03.2021, police
had prior information, based on which, at 01:45 PM, a
Scooty was intercepted by the police and the applicant

2
was arrested. In fact, it is the case that the applicant
obstructed the police party in discharging their duties. It
is alleged that Narcotic substances was also recovered in
huge quantity from the applicant. Thereafter, at the
instance of the applicant, the police proceeded and one
more person Amaan was also arrested. The FIR records
that the recovery memo was prepared in the street light
and police party left the place of occurrence at 08:30 PM.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit
that the entire case is false; police had already apprehended
the applicant; he was seen in the CCTV footages of the
police station on multiple occasions; on 15.03.2021, at
about 04:27 PM, the applicant is seen entering into the
police station; he is also been seen in the CCTV footages at
about at 06:21 PM; a person entered the police station in a
black Scooty bearing Registration No.UK08 AC 8099. He
would submit that there are other CCTV footages also which
establishes the applicant was in police station in the
afternoon of 15.03.2021 whereas, as per police, they left the
place of incident at 08:30 PM in the evening and reached at
police station at 04:37 AM on 16.03.2021, when the FIR
was lodged.

3
6. It is further argued that subsequent to filing of
charge-sheet, the applicant had filed a petition for quashing
the proceeding under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973, in which, the Court had sought a report
from SSP Haridwar on CCTV footages and SSP Haridwar
had confirmed those CCTV footages. It is argued that it is
an additional material after rejection of the first bail
application; in addition to it, it is also argued that the trial
has been stayed; applicant is in custody for a long.
7. Learned State counsel would submit that the
question of CCTV footages cannot be raised again and
again. The plea with regard to CCTV footages and presence
of the applicant in the police station in the afternoon of
15.03.2021 had already been taken in the first bail
application and the State had admitted all those averments
in the counter affidavit.
8. It is argued that now, those pleas are not
available to the applicant; there is no changed
circumstance. But, it is argued that the applicant seeks
review of his earlier bail order.
9. It is true that bail, once rejected, the same issue
may not be permitted to be raised again and again. The bail
order may not be reviewed. But, the question that fall for

4
consideration in this matter is, is it a case of any changed
circumstance?
10. The first bail rejection order dated 18.11.2021,
passed in BA1 No. 1000 of 2021, reveals that the presence
of applicant at police station in the afternoon of 15.03.2021
was verified from the Police Inspector and in para 6 of the
bail rejection order, the Court observed as hereunder:-
"6. The informant Manender Singh Rana is also
present before the Court at the time of hearing on the
bail application, who disclosed that when they reached
at the spot accused Javed committed marpeet with the
team; accordingly, they took the accused at the police
station on the very same day; and, thereafter, they
prepared the recovery memo of two incidents
mentioned in the recovery memo."
11. After discussing the arguments and the facts in
para 7 of the bail rejection order, the court observed,
"whether the contraband article were planted by the
arresting team against the accused or not it is a matter
of evidence; the Court cannot assess the entire facts at
this stage". Something has definitely changed thereafter. In
C-482 No.336 of 2022, Javed Ali vs. State of Uttarakhand
and another, this Court passed an order on 22.03.2022,
keeping in view the CCTV footages; the SSP Haridwar was

5
required to submit a report. The details have been
submitted by the SSP Haridwar. This order and the report is
part of this record.
12. The FIR records that at 01:45 PM the applicant's
Scooty was intercepted. This Court has now, advantage of
verification of the entire statement as made by the
applicant. It is not the CCTV footages alone, but SSP
Haridwar has given the details, as to what contained in
those CCTV footages. This is now additional material before
this Court. The CCTV footages categorically reveals that on
15.03.2021, the Drug Inspector, police and the applicant
were in the police station premises. One of the important
CCTV footages is of 06:29:10, in which, a person has been
seen entering into the police station in a black Scooty
No.UK08 AC 8099. It is important that as per G.D. Report
No.4 dated 16.03.2021, 4:57 AM, of the concerned police
station, Scooty was allegedly recovered from the applicant
and was lodged in the police station. Does not, this CCTV
footages falsify the entire prosecution story on this point?
Perhaps, it will fall for scrutiny during trial. There are
changed circumstances, which entitles the applicant to bail.
13. Having considered, this Court is of the view
that it is a case fit for bail and the applicant deserves to
be enlarged on bail.

6
14. The bail application is allowed.
15. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his
executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable
sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the
court concerned.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 23.03.2023
Sanjay
